prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To generate a real damages range I would need: (1) Womack's total medical specials to date (ER, hospitalization, right knee surgery costs, any future left knee surgery estimate); (2) any wage-loss or lost-earning-capacity figures; (3) a life-care-plan or future-medical-cost projection if one exists given the bilateral knee replacement need; (4) the specific dollar amount of Mississippi's applicable statutory noneconomic damages cap as it would apply to this claim; and (5) any settlement demand, mediation figure, or jury verdict amount actually placed in the record.
prediction.likelyOutcome: On this record Womack is well-positioned to win liability (dangerous condition plus actual/constructive notice through the GM's proximity) and to establish causation for at least the aggravation of her preexisting bilateral osteoarthritis necessitating knee replacement, with the meniscal-tear-specific causation somewhat more contested but bolstered by Dr. Hosemann's clarifying affidavit. No dollar recovery figure can be estimated from this record, however, because no medical bills, wage-loss, life-care costs, settlement demand, or verdict figures appear anywhere in the materials, and any noneconomic award will be trimmed by Mississippi's statutory cap in an amount this record does not state.

issues.label: Existence of an unreasonably dangerous condition (collapsed wet-floor sign)
Actual/constructive notice to Pilot (via GM Franklin)
Causation of knee injuries (meniscal tears and need for bilateral knee replacement)
Comparative fault / failure to observe the hazard
Admissibility of Dr. Hosemann's clarifying affidavit (sham-affidavit exposure)

outcome.description: The jury found the defendants' negligence the sole proximate cause of the fall and awarded $393,000 in economic damages (past and future medical expenses) and $3,000,000 in noneconomic damages. The circuit court reduced the noneconomic award to the $1,000,000 statutory cap (Miss. Code Ann. 11-1-60(2)(b)), entering an amended final judgment for $1,393,000, and denied JNOV or new trial. The Court of Appeals of Mississippi, en banc, affirmed on December 17, 2024, rejecting the dangerous-condition, notice, expert and further-remittitur arguments. No attorney's fees.
